artDirection: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide landscape project-card cover for an algorithm learning website. Minimal editorial still life, tactile matte cut-paper and ceramic forms on warm ivory paper, muted sage, charcoal and sand, soft natural shadows, sophisticated understated design. One simple central composition with generous margins and very few objects; landscape 3:2 composition. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, neon, gradients, glossy plastic, robots, computers or interface mockups. Subject:

routelab.subject: A tiny architectural maze of low sand-colored walls, with a single olive thread finding a path from one small charcoal pebble to another.

crossword.subject: A small square arrangement of ivory letterless crossword tiles, a few charcoal blank squares and one sage tile, viewed from above.

delivery.subject: Three tiny matte buildings connected by a winding olive cord, one charcoal parcel at the center, an abstract delivery network.

transit.subject: A folded ivory transit map with two thin crossing sage lines and three small charcoal station discs, plus a tiny sand clock disc without numbers.

binary-quest.subject: Eight matte ivory and charcoal circular tokens in a single neat row, one olive token hovering slightly above the row, representing a binary practice puzzle.

cpp-toolkit.subject: Two parallel rows of five matte ceramic bars, one unordered and one ascending, ivory and sage with one charcoal bar, elegant sorting comparison.

huffman.subject: A broad folded strip of ivory paper narrowing into a compact sage accordion, symbolizing lossless compression, with a very subtle branching thread beside it.

go-workbench.subject: A charcoal pivot pebble dividing a small cluster of low sage ceramic rods from taller sand rods, a spare abstract quicksort still life.

go-journey.subject: Two separate small stacks of pale paper strips merging into a single orderly stack in the foreground, symbolizing merge sort.

go-ranges.subject: A linear row of eight ivory rectangular blocks, a sage bracket-like paper strip covering the central four blocks, a range sum still life.

go-collections.subject: A balanced miniature pyramid of seven matte ceramic spheres, the small charcoal sphere at the top, sage lower spheres, an abstract min heap.

go-prefix.subject: Three delicate olive branches emerging from one charcoal trunk, each ending in a tiny ivory square tile, a shared-prefix trie sculptural diagram.

graphforge.subject: Three layered translucent vellum squares with subtly different thin olive node-and-edge paths, slightly offset, representing versions of one network.

python-structures.subject: A spare balanced branching tree made from slim charcoal rods and seven sage circular ceramic nodes on ivory paper.

number-system.subject: A neat set of four low matte sand blocks doubling in width from left to right, a single charcoal token beside them, abstract binary place values.

similarity.subject: Two overlapping ivory paper sheets with matching short charcoal strokes and one shared muted sage highlighted strip, abstract source-code similarity, no actual text.

cashflow.subject: Three shallow matte ceramic dishes containing small sand discs, with one olive disc between two dishes, an understated balanced expense settlement.

streamshield.subject: A narrow stream of sand pebbles passing through a sage rectangular paper frame, a single charcoal pebble outside the frame, representing an event-time window.

strings.subject: A long thin ivory paper ribbon with a repeating pattern of charcoal dots and dashes, one short repeat framed by a sage cut-paper loop, abstract string pattern matching.

retrieval.subject: A small group of upright ivory index cards in a low sand tray, one sage card pulled slightly forward beneath a charcoal circular magnifier ring.

bitrealm.subject: A single row of eight small ceramic toggle-like squares alternating charcoal and ivory, one sage square rotated out of alignment, abstract eight-bit operations.

delivery: WebP at up to 960×640, quality 88; generated source images preserved in the image generation output directory.
